findings.title: Edit campaign's Apply writes every clock field as the form drew it at open, so a clock moved while the window stands is put back
findings.where: scripts/gm-campaign.mjs:217, 223 (drawn once), 347-361 (the patch over the clock), 281-283 (the comment); the same rows and Apply run Season setup's Save (season-setup.mjs:827, 1250)
findings.what_happens: The window reads the clock once (217) and has no keepLive. Apply hands applyCampaignForm the form's name, chapter, day, phase, session and time of day, and the patch (347-354) carries all six to setClock (361), which spreads it over the clock as it is then. If the time of day advanced, an Eclipse ended, a body moved the phase to Investigation or a trial began while the window stood, Apply writes the old values back: the time of day goes back, and correctsTheHour (357) reads the rewind as a correction and calls off a called assembly. The phase question asks only on a move into the Class Trial (322), so a stale Investigation written over a running trial leaves the trial without a question. `moved` (363-365) compares against the clock read at Apply, so the Eclipse warning fires but nothing says the clock went back. The comment at 281-283 records that "it is not a live window" and only the warning was made to read the clock at the write.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens Edit campaign (or Season setup) to fix the campaign name, another GM or the HUD's chevron moves the Morning to the Afternoon, and the first GM's Apply puts the clock back to the Morning, calling off the assembly called for the Afternoon, with no word that the time moved.
findings.expected: the window redrawn when the clock changes (the fields not being typed in), or Apply writing only the fields the GM changed
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a redraw or a dirty-field filter: openClockDialog has no render hook beyond End the chapter (224-230); readClockForm (82-94) reads every field; applyCampaignForm writes the patch whole. setClock (clock.mjs:135-160) spreads the patch over the clock read in its step, so nothing restores the newer fields. The tier 2 tests named in the comments set the form and press Apply on a clock that did not move meanwhile. Edit campaign alone is reached only by game.drpg.editClock (api.mjs:383); Season setup's window, where the same rows and Apply stand, is the ordinary door - not read here (another reader's surface).
findings.probe: Open game.drpg.editClock(); from a second GM call game.drpg.advanceTimeOfDay() (or advance from the HUD); press Apply on the first: read getClock().timeOfDay before and after
